"Confirmed — Flagged set contains 17 annual renewals (term_days=365): 8 from DLR-104 ($723.42) and 9 from DLR-219 ($782.87). Effective dates span 1–28 May 2026; posted 31 May 2026."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment

"100% of annual-plan records dataset-wide have matching effective and posting months (effective_month == posting_month). Zero annual records have posted_at earlier than effective_event_date."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Unknowns and Decision-Changing Evidence"
"Revenue-Recognition Policy: Resolving evidence: GL revenue policy manual... if upfront recognition on posted_at is required, this evidence would change my decision to escalate to Finance."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do NOT hold transactions or reverse postings. Implement a read-only trend dashboard reporting volume by `effective_event_date` alongside `posted_at` to eliminate apparent month-end spikes."
"Perform read-only verification of GL accounting rules, dealer contracts, and entitlement logs."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "No material issue; do not escalate the 31 May cluster as duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, period stuffing, or a pipeline defect."
"Reversibility: This action is 100% reversible, read-only, and zero-risk—it makes zero mutations, holds, or deletions to production ledgers."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "fully supported by recharge data, match dealer import logs, and align with historical operational practices" is somewhat broader than the evidence because entitlement activation, contractual transmission requirements, and revenue-recognition policy were not yet verified.

"proving routine batching rather than an unprecedented May surge" overstates what historical counts and the sixth-ranked daily volume establish; they corroborate a recurring pattern but do not prove the absence of manipulation or every possible pipeline issue.

"Pipeline defect / Data corruption — rejected based on evidence" is well supported for duplicate ingestion and cash-to-ledger reconciliation, but the tests do not rule out all upstream or downstream data defects.
"zero-risk" is too absolute even for a read-only dashboard, although the proposed action is operationally low risk.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst appropriately considered duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, period stuffing, and pipeline defects, while also identifying revenue-policy, contract, entitlement, and region-mapping alternatives. The main incompletely tested alternative is that effective_event_date values could be wrong or altered upstream, meaning month-level alignment and historical batching would not alone establish the true event timing.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run and document the entitlement reconciliation for each flagged source_event_id, alongside an explicit check of the GL recognition policy and dealer contracts; this would close the largest remaining gap between reconciled postings and the broader conclusion of no material issue.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Pre-authentication termination is 24.0% under NOVA (650/2,709) vs 7.9% under LEGACY, driven by TOKEN_MISMATCH (200) and ANI_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT (146)."
"Containment dashboard excludes pre-auth sessions (73.9% reported vs 56.1% true all-contact rate across 2,709 sessions)."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "Authentication failures (200 TOKEN_MISMATCH, 146 ANI_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT) cause sessions to terminate pre-auth and disappear from CareDesk complaint metrics."
"Causal claims (tentative): Authentication defects and suppressed case creation explain the decline, while genuine self-service handles simple queries."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Self-service alone caused complaint reduction — rejected."
"Remaining unknowns: 72-hour repeat contact rates across channels, fix timelines for OrbitBill timeouts, and downstream resolution of outage-affected callers."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand nationally yet. Continue South pilot as a reversible controlled test."
"If repeat contacts exceed 10%, execute an immediate rollback of South back to LEGACY IVR."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Hold national expansion, execute a targeted pull of OrbitBill logs to reconcile 650 pre-auth dropouts against CareDesk cases, and sample 100 calls across self-service and auth failures."
"What rule triggers automatic CareDesk case creation or agent transfer in NOVA, and how does it handle unauthenticated callers facing technical errors?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Complaints and faults moved in opposite directions, proving complaints went quiet from IVR measurement suppression rather than fewer issues." The evidence supports a measurement-failure hypothesis, but service events and ticket counts alone do not prove that explanation or establish that affected customers would have complained.

"pre-auth defects suppressed case logging across all South contact paths." The IVR evidence supports missing case creation for affected IVR sessions, not suppression across App, Dealer, and Agent channels; the non-IVR decline has not been mechanistically explained.

"Authentication failures (200 TOKEN_MISMATCH, 146 ANI_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT) cause sessions to terminate pre-auth." The records appear consistent with this mechanism, but the submission does not show exception or retry evidence establishing causality, and those two categories total only 346 of the 650 pre-auth terminations.

"CareDesk case creation rate collapsed from 49.5% to 3.3% under NOVA, eliminating complaint logging opportunities." It shows a major measurement risk, but 'eliminating' is too absolute and the submission does not specify the denominator or whether all relevant case-creation pathways were assessed.

"If repeat contacts >15%, rollback pilot" and "If repeat contacts exceed 10%, execute an immediate rollback." These thresholds are presented without a baseline, rationale, or demonstrated decision relevance.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission appropriately handles the strongest alternative that genuine self-service reduced some simple contacts while the measured complaint decline was partly caused by failed case creation. It misses a plausible benign explanation for the 53.3% South non-IVR decline, such as changes in contact volume, customer mix, seasonality, or channel routing, and it treats high service-event exposure as evidence of expected complaints without linking affected accounts to journeys or repeat contacts.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the asserted causal language with an explicit end-to-end validation plan that links IVR sessions, case creation, repeat contacts, service-event-affected accounts, and sampled call outcomes; specifically distinguish abandonment from complaint and resolution before attributing the ticket decline to capture failure.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission specifically cites inverter_events.csv and identifies the fields impact_mw = 0, cleared = yes, inverter IDs, dates, and durations.
The claim that these records establish no 'active plant emergency' is broader than the cited extract supports; the submission itself acknowledges unknown filtering and fleet scope.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission distinguishes event labels from proven physical failure or commercial loss and proposes checking whether the extract omitted uncleared or nonzero-impact events.
The analysis relies on one summarized CSV and does not independently cross-check SCADA, historian, fleet status, or event semantics before making its high-confidence rejection.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It appropriately states that total fleet size and filtering parameters are unknown and proposes a specific scope check.
The high-confidence statement that the evidence refutes 'active inverter hardware failure' is overbroad: four cleared zero-impact records do not rule out a transient or unrecorded hardware issue.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to 'hold escalation and perform a single cheap SCADA/historian log query' is proportionate and decision-linked.
The proposed query is discriminating: it checks for omitted uncleared events or capacity losses, with escalation conditional on finding them.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly avoids inventing a plant problem from four short, cleared, zero-impact records and preserves a low-cost scope check.

It is somewhat over-scoped in rejecting hardware failure, operator intent, or commercial loss as hypotheses rather than limiting the conclusion to no evidence of persistent operational impact in this extract.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: 'Event strings ... establish only that software threshold alerts were logged' is not established by the CSV fields as presented; the strings may be event classifications, but their software-threshold semantics require documentation or corroboration.
'The evidence refutes ... active inverter hardware failure' overstates what cleared zero-impact records can show; they do not exclude transient hardware faults or faults omitted by filtering.
'Showing ... no ... active plant emergency' is broader than the extract supports, especially because the submission acknowledges unknown filtering criteria and fleet size.
'No inverter exhibits recurring faults' is true only within this four-record extract, not necessarily for the plant or the full observation period.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: These may be benign, transient telemetry or communications-quality events with no observed generation impact, but the extract could also be a filtered subset that omits active trips, repeated events, or nonzero-loss records. The evidence supports pausing escalation while checking scope, not a definitive rejection of all equipment-related explanations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Narrow the conclusion from 'hardware failure ... refuted' to 'no persistent hardware or commercial impact is evidenced in this extract,' and execute the proposed SCADA/historian scope query to verify whether uncleared, repeated, or nonzero-impact events were excluded.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "I independently recomputed the block-level arithmetic across all 768 rows in dispatch_blocks.csv" and reports the specific 28 May and 29 May MWh and penalty totals.
"Recomputing the same-day counterfactual by applying base_schedule_mw to 29 May actuals" directly uses the required fields and reports the resulting penalty and deviation differences.
The evidence table identifies dispatch_blocks.csv, AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md, and DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf for the principal claims.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission distinguishes the uncontrolled 28 May versus 29 May comparison from the same-day base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw counterfactual.
It checks gross versus net deviation, calm-day baseline variation, alternative conventional days, firmware differences, and block-level recovery behavior.
It identifies that only 12 of 96 blocks were revised and isolates Blocks 63–64 as a potentially adverse recovery case.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "The 31.6% figure is arithmetically reproducible, but it should not be presented as the causal effect of the pilot."
The submission explicitly identifies unknown gate-closure timestamps and uncertainty about incremental value over Firmware 4.8.
It states decision-changing evidence for both timely ex-ante submission and late submission, rather than treating the computed counterfactual as conclusive causal proof.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to hold expansion, retain the tool only in reversible shadow mode, and keep conventional dispatch on the live grid follows from the limited causal evidence and identified timing uncertainty.
The proposed next test controls firmware conditions, samples 10 high-wind events, records timestamps, and measures both DSM penalty and net commercial value.
The recommendation includes explicit continuation and pull criteria and corrects the internal note rather than discarding the pilot outright.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: "What survives as the narrower defensible claim is an ex-post 17.55% penalty reduction on the 12 revised blocks of this pilot day under Firmware 4.7, not a general 31.6% reduction."
The conclusion preserves a smaller same-day benefit while rejecting the unsupported claim that the cross-day 31.6% figure is causal.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Calling 28 May "cherry-picked" implies intent that is not established by the supplied evidence; the evidence supports that it was an unusually unfavorable comparator and that the comparison is selection-sensitive, not that it was deliberately cherry-picked.

The statement that natural wind variability "exceeds pilot effect size" is not demonstrated by the cited 4 June comparison alone: the reported 4 June penalty difference from the 29 May pilot day is smaller than the derived same-day difference, and firmware also differs.
The "exact within-day reduction" is an exact arithmetic result under a modeled same-actuals counterfactual, not a fully identified causal effect; actual outcomes under the base schedule could differ.

The proposed thresholds of a mean reduction of at least 12%, at least 8 of 10 events, and less than 5% for pulling the tool are decision rules rather than evidence-derived thresholds, though they are appropriately framed as a future test plan.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot may have produced a real but smaller operational benefit on 29 May, while much of the 31.6% cross-day result reflects unusually severe wind conditions on 28 May, ordinary event-to-event variability, and possibly firmware differences. The same-day 17.55% modeled saving is evidence of potential value, but it remains an ex-post counterfactual rather than a controlled causal estimate.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Audit gate-closure and revision-submission timestamps, then run the proposed matched high-wind evaluation with Firmware 4.8 held constant and pre-specified base-versus-pilot scoring. This would test both ex-ante usability and incremental value while avoiding the cross-day comparator problem.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Declared tariff code is 90211000 for item P1001 on filing date 2025-11-04 | declaration.pdf"
"90211000 is the Swiss working classification for P1001 effective 2025-01-01 | country_tariff_matrix.xlsx (Swiss Matrix)"
"Extraction schema strips punctuation/pads strings but does not model code-system identifier, nomenclature version, or effective dates | canonical-schema-v0.3.md"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "90211000 exactly matches the Swiss working tariff matrix classification defined for P1001"
"A raw string mismatch proves a declaration error: Rejected because comparing cross-jurisdiction nomenclatures without a code-system translation layer produces systemic false positives."
"This evidence would change my decision to escalate if official Tares legally mandates an 8-digit line other than 90211000"

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Do NOT escalate as a likely declaration error."
"Official Swiss Tares tariff line or binding tariff decision for P1001" is identified as missing.
"Broker classification workpapers" and "Pipeline code-system metadata" are also identified as unresolved evidence.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Switzerland uses Swiss local tariff (Tares); EU uses CN8, so matching 8-digit strings across jurisdictions is not expected"
"Both declared 90211000 and Helios 90211090 share the 6-digit root HS6 902110"
"Extraction schema strips punctuation/pads strings but does not model code-system identifier, nomenclature version, or effective dates"

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Hold escalation on this declaration pending automated rule suppression"
"rather than routing individual false positives upward or issuing"
"Resolve by obtaining Broker BRK-A's legal classification rationale"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "90211000 is the verified Swiss working tariff classification" is stronger than the submission's own evidence warrants because it lacks an official Swiss Tares tariff line or binding tariff decision.

"Both codes share the common WCO 6-digit root HS6 902110. Switzerland uses national Swiss Tares codes rather than EU CN8; therefore, exact 8-digit string comparison ... generates a false positive control flag" is well-supported as a likely explanation, but "false positive" is not conclusively established until the official tariff and product-specification evidence are checked.

"pending automated rule suppression" proposes suppressing a control before the identified legal and broker evidence is resolved; a scoped hold, quarantine, or corrected code-system-aware rule would be safer.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The mismatch is probably a benign Swiss-versus-EU nomenclature mismatch, but the declared code could still be incorrect if the matrix is not legally authoritative, is outdated, or does not match P1001's technical specifications. The submission itself identifies the missing official Tares decision and broker workpapers that could support this alternative.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the broad proposed rule suppression with a reversible, narrowly scoped quarantine and obtain the official BAZG/Tares result plus broker classification rationale before treating the declaration as definitively non-escalatable.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "P1006 is declared with Preference = Yes and 0.0% duty on 2025-09-18, but no supplier support is linked in ClearView"
"Central register lookup returns no active document reference for SUP-02 / P1006 on 2025-09-18 (record expired 2025-07-31)"
"Register search explicit disclaimer confirms absence of a current reference does not prove that no document exists outside the register"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "US manufacturing origin in ERP/Invoice disproves preferential origin." Rejected because ERP/Invoice reflects non-preferential manufacturing location, whereas preferential origin is governed by specific trade agreement rules, processing, and supplier declarations.

"No current document in the central register means no valid document exists." Rejected because the register search explicitly warns that documents exist outside the register and Procurement confirms they reside in category folders.
"Unsupported and false are distinct verdicts."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The correct status is 'unsupported / not established', not 'false'"
"the central supplier register is known to be incomplete, and valid supplier declarations frequently exist outside it in Procurement category folders"
"preference cannot be granted now, but the claim cannot be definitively ruled non-originating without checking category records"

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "ERP/Helios carries physical manufacturing country and was never designed to establish preferential origin or rule compliance"
"Procurement confirms supplier declarations sit in category folders and the central register is not always updated when sourcing routes change"
"Actual Sourcing Supplier Identification for this shipment" is identified as missing, with purchase orders and batch traceability proposed to resolve it.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible administrative hold on granting the preferential tariff claim rather than making an irrevocable filing or fraud referral."
"Request the current supplier declaration from Procurement category folders and ask the customs broker for the specific origin rule invoked."
"Clear the consignment provisionally under standard MFN duty terms (or duty guarantee) while evidence is gathered."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "If found valid, this would change the decision to approving preferential origin (0% duty)" is too broad: a supplier declaration alone may not establish preferential origin without confirming the applicable agreement, origin criterion, classification and transaction facts.

"If confirmed non-existent, it would change the decision to permanently rejecting preference" overstates what missing documentation establishes; it may justify rejecting preference for this entry, but does not necessarily establish permanent non-originating status.

"Clear the consignment provisionally under standard MFN duty terms" is generally proportionate, but the submission does not cite the applicable customs procedure or confirm that provisional MFN clearance or a duty guarantee is legally and operationally available.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The claim may be valid but unsupported in the reviewed systems: a current supplier declaration could exist in Procurement category folders, and the US manufacturing information may describe physical manufacture rather than preferential origin. Conversely, even if a declaration is found, the claim still requires confirmation of the applicable trade agreement and origin rule.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify the applicable trade agreement, tariff classification and origin criterion alongside the supplier declaration and shipment sourcing records before stating that any document would automatically establish or permanently reject preferential origin.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "qc_release_sop.md: 'Service target'" and the quoted 24-hour clock-start definition; "batch_release.csv: 17 column headers"; exact counts and percentages for HOLD records and 02:10:00 clustering; "source_freshness.csv: rows 2-4".
The submission triangulates SOP text, batch fields, timestamp distributions, and freshness metadata, while also identifying the relevant counterevidence and limitations.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The apparent ~1.5-day cycle time cannot be used as a KPI due to four verified defects" followed by separate tests of clock-start semantics, censoring from active HOLDs, timestamp clustering, and source cadence.
"Sample 20 batches against live QCore transaction audit logs (sys_audit) to extract exact user disposition timestamps instead of source_snapshot_ts (02:10:00)."
The reasoning distinguishes the observed metric from the underlying workflow and identifies audit-log evidence that would discriminate interface timing from true disposition timing.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Material Unknown 1: Existence of Computable Input Fields" and the conditional decision branches for whether timestamp fields exist in source logs.
"Material Unknown 2: True transactional disposition event timestamps" with explicit alternative outcomes based on audit-log results.

The submission operationally bounds several uncertainties, but labels some inferences as "verified defects" and gives them high confidence even where the evidence establishes risk or extract limitation rather than definitive system behavior.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Yes, verify the extract and halt building the dashboard" and "The smallest, cheapest verification is checking whether source systems capture the required inputs before building pipelines."

The recommendation reframes the task from dashboard construction to metric feasibility, proposes a small reversible verification, and specifies how the decision changes if source timestamps or audit evidence are found.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Rejected Hypotheses" tests receipt-to-release as the KPI, actual queue turnaround, 02:10:00 as transactional time, and lab completion as an evidence-availability proxy.
"For this to survive" statements explicitly state what would have to be true for each competing explanation to remain viable.
The strongest alternatives are addressed with evidence, and future evidence that could revive them is identified.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Verify whether source systems (CertVault, QMS, LabTrack) log timestamped evidence completion events"; "Sample 20 batches against live QCore transaction audit logs"; and "Review deviation logs for the 42 HOLD batches."
These are prioritized, decision-linked requests for the smallest high-value evidence rather than a generic request for more data.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Calling the four issues "verified defects" overstates the evidence: missing fields are verified in the extract, but not necessarily absent from the underlying source systems.
"Upstream extracts have divergent refresh cycles ... introducing artificial cross-system lag" establishes a comparability risk, not proof that the reported lag is artificial.
The statement that "true median queue time exceeds 72 hours" is imprecise: 72.54 hours is the median current age of unreleased HOLD records, not necessarily the median completed queue-cycle time.
The 02:10:00 concentration strongly supports interface or snapshot timing, but does not by itself prove the timestamps are synthetic rather than actual commits at that time.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10:00 values may be legitimate QCore interface commits or batch-release posting times rather than fabricated timestamps, and the apparent lag may partly reflect genuine workflow delay. Transaction audit logs and event-level evidence timestamps are needed to distinguish these mechanisms.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Soften the four "verified defects" into explicitly separated observations, risks, and hypotheses, especially for timestamp semantics and source desynchronization; then make the primary gate a prioritized audit-log sample that simultaneously tests true disposition time and source-snapshot timing.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “spare_parts.csv: rows 2–4 (MTR-4401), 5–7 (PMP-2288), 11–14 (VLV-3722)”
“part_requests.csv: rows 2, 6, 11, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 21, 22, 25 (null MPN)”
“source_freshness.csv: row 6 (MaintStar-global 2026-06-26); maintenance_email.txt”

The submission gives unusually specific file, row, and field references and distinguishes actionable, needs-check, and not-transferable candidates. However, some broad conclusions such as “Description variance is cosmetic” and “MPN is ground truth” extend beyond the cited examples, and counterevidence about UOM and other restriction fields is not shown.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: “The root cause of duplicate spend is not catalog description variance, but poor data discipline (missing MPNs), 55-day stale global inventory snapshots, and local critical-asset reservation locks.”
“Text similarity alone is sufficient for matching: Rejected — ... pure text matching produces false positives.”

The submission identifies several plausible mechanisms and correctly separates identity, revision, reservation, and freshness concerns. But it does not demonstrate that description variance is not a material contributor, and the cited HEPA example shows similar descriptions rather than a tested false-positive case. It also jumps from these mechanisms to rejecting the semantic-search pilot, despite semantic retrieval being useful for generating candidates when confirmation controls are applied.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “~11% ... is actionable now; ~25% ... needs engineering revision/reservation check; and ~64% ... represents insufficient evidence”
“Actionable now” for PMP-2288, BRG-1507, and PLC-8840
“Global inventory snapshot is 55 days stale”

The categorical buckets and explicit “needs check” treatment are useful, and the stale snapshot is recognized. However, “actionable now” remains too strong for enterprise data that may be temporally inconsistent, and the submission does not quantify how stale data, missing MPNs, UOM, qualification, or restrictions affect the confidence of each candidate. “MPN is the reliable identity key” is overstated as a complete transferability rule.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: “Leadership should reject the semantic-search pilot.”
“Live local CMMS stock & reservation balances”
“If live data confirms stock is truly unreserved, I will decide to cancel PR-260712 ... and transfer stock; if confirmed reserved, I will decide to approve the external PO.”

The submission usefully reframes candidate value versus actionable value and proposes engineering, reservation, and qualification gates. But rejecting the pilot is not supported by the evidence: the evidence supports semantic search as candidate generation with confirmation, not abandonment. Conditional cancellation or PO approval is also operationally consequential and should require current availability, revision, UOM, qualification, and reservation confirmation rather than only a live balance check.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: “All positive available_qty is freely transferable: Rejected”
“Revision difference is minor: Rejected”
“Blank-MPN requests are matchable now: Rejected”

The submission actively tests several important unsafe assumptions against the policy, restrictions, email, and freshness data. It does not seriously test the strongest competing interpretation—that semantic search can still provide high-value candidate generation despite poor source data—or establish that description variance is merely cosmetic rather than a risk requiring normalization and engineering confirmation.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: “Planners pull live CMMS screen balances for HA-0022, ME-0006, RI-0001, ME-0003, and HA-0012.”
“Maintenance planners inspect equipment nameplates and populate the mandatory manufacturer_part_no field”
“Central Plant Engineering issues a formal backward-compatibility ruling for MTR-4401 and VLV-3722.”

The requested evidence is prioritized and tied to explicit decision changes, especially live reservation balances and formal revision rulings. It would be stronger if it specified a consistent point-in-time reconciliation across request, inventory, reservation, and restriction extracts, and if it prioritized the smallest pilot validation for semantic candidate recall and precision.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Leadership should reject the semantic-search pilot” is not supported; the evidence supports controlled semantic candidate generation with MPN, engineering, qualification, reservation, and freshness confirmation.
“Description variance is cosmetic” is generalized from a few same-MPN examples and ignores descriptions that may encode revision, UOM, qualification, or application details.

“MPN is ground truth” is too absolute: MPN is strong identity evidence but does not establish transferability or suitability without revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, and current availability checks.

The statement that “pure text matching produces false positives” is not demonstrated by the cited HEPA example, which shows similar descriptions for the same part rather than an actual false-positive match.
“Local critical-asset reservation locks” is presented as a root cause broadly, although the cited reservation evidence appears limited to particular rows and parts.
The proposed $77.6k drive/valve transfer opportunity is not reconciled to the candidate values shown in the table, so its calculation and scope are unclear.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The evidence supports a controlled semantic-search pilot rather than rejection: normalize descriptions and use semantic similarity to generate candidates, then require MPN confirmation where available, nameplate or planner verification where absent, revision/UOM/qualification and reservation checks, and a fresh local/global availability reconciliation before any transfer. Poor MPN completeness and stale inventory reduce actionable value and confidence, but they do not show that candidate-generation search is ineffective.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a small, reversible pilot on the listed PRs using semantic retrieval plus mandatory engineering and availability gates, with a point-in-time reconciliation of MaintStar, local CMMS reservations, restrictions, revisions, UOM, and qualifications; measure candidate precision, confirmed transferable value, and false-transfer rate before deciding whether to scale or stop.
